**Summary:** The schema it built over MCP is sound: 4 blocks (hero, rich text, image, quote) in one shared block grid, with the page and block types in the right folders. The rendering code follows the project's conventions exactly. But the model stopped partway through debugging and left the site broken in two ways. A stray debugging copy of a page template breaks the build, and all the block content is set up so that no blocks would render even if it built.

**Top issues:**
1. **Major:** `dotnet build` fails with error CS0246 because of `Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco/wwwroot/Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml`. The model copied the front page template there to test where Umbraco looks for templates, and never deleted it. Umbraco doesn't start, so I couldn't crawl the site or take screenshots, and none exist for this run.
2. **Major:** On the front page and both posts, every block is listed with an all-zero ID, so Umbraco skips them all and the pages render with no blocks. The model found this itself near the end of the run.
3. **Major:** The session ended on an interim message: "Now I'll re-save the value with expose entries and verify they persist:". That fix never happened, and the message doesn't mention the broken build, so the final report scored 0 of 2.
4. **Minor:** Each post would show its photo and title twice: once in the page header and again in the hero block.
5. **Minor:** The ViewComponent classes sit in `Models/Blocks/`, and the text block's view model depends on an Umbraco type. Scratch files (`.tmp_*`, `.front.html`, `.post1.html`) were left in the solution root.

The posts themselves are on topic and accurate (about 620 and 525 words, with relevant photos), and the run used only MCP in the expected order. `grade.json` and `grade.md` are in the run folder, and the grade appears in `npm run report`. The reset archived the solution as `refs/runs/2026-10-09_2124_mcp_glm-5.3-flash-high`, and `npm run status` reports **pristine**.
